fusion_ranked_evidence.title: CJP's parliament march from Jantar Mantar: India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown - BBC
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown. Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban. Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained. Police and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government have not commented on the use of sticks and tear gas against protesters. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people turning up from all over the country to participate in the CJP's call to march to parliament on the opening day of the monsoon session.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Indian 'CJP' to continue Delhi demonstrations against education minister - The Jerusalem Post
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: ## Thousands of protesters from Delhi and nearby cities and towns gathered to march on parliament on Monday, joining a movement that began as online satire. A supporter of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) poses while holding the Indian national flag at a protest site, a day after thousands of protesters marched toward parliament demanding the resignation of the Education Minister over examination paper leaks, at Jantar Mantar in India, July 21, 2026. India's youth-led "cockroach" movement said on Tuesday it would continue its protest but will not march again, a day after scores of supporters were injured in clashes with police who tried to stop their march on parliament. Delhi Police said nearly 180 people, including 118 security and police personnel, and 60 protesters, were injured on Monday when they clashed in central Delhi. Thousands of protesters from Delhi and nearby cities and towns gathered to march on parliament on Monday, joining a movement that began as online satire but has become the biggest challenge for Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his third term.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Indian police forcibly hospitalize Cockroach Janata Party activist on hunger strike - Los Angeles Times
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: * Police in New Delhi forcibly moved education reform activist Sonam Wangchuk to a hospital after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike. NEW DELHI — Police forcibly transferred a prominent activist to a hospital in New Delhi on Saturday after his health deteriorated during a 20-day hunger strike tied to India’s Cockroach Janata Party movement for education reform. Delhi police said that Wangchuk was taken to the hospital after his health worsened during the hunger strike and that a brief commotion occurred when some protesters tried to block the move. The Cockroach Janata Party — a play on the name of India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party — said in a social media post that the government “forcefully abducted” Wangchuk “without his or his family’s consent” two days before their planned march to India’s Parliament.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Trump administration drive to seize election powers sparking ‘chaos’ despite pushback - The Guardian
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: US courts, state officials and Democrats warn that moves are endangering voting rights and the rule of law. The Trump administration continues to expand its authoritarian and radical drive to revamp voting rules and seize state election powers, though it faces growing resistance from US courts, state officials and Democrats, who warn the moves are sparking “chaos” and endangering voting rights and the rule of law. Donald Trump’s unprecedented drive to change election rules, which states legally set, is fueled by his obsession with his 2020 election loss to Joe Biden, which he falsely attributes to voting fraud, coupled with his fear that Democrats will “find a reason to impeach me” if they take control of the House in November’s midterms elections, say former election officials and legal experts. Given Trump’s dark mindset, his administration has used justice department legal moves and threats, FBI raids and investigations, and other federal agencies to coerce states to change voting rules in key ways, including curtailing voting by mail and machines that Trump and Maga allies have vilified, baselessly, as riddled with fraud.

NEW DELHI, July 23 (Reuters) - Youth protesters demanding the education minister's resignation clashed briefly with police on the streets of New Delhi late on Wednesday, ‌with officers firing tear gas and wielding canes to push them back, police and witnesses said. fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Agriculture students at loggerheads with govt over AO, AAO recruitment - Deccan Herald
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Agriculture students at loggerheads with govt over AO, AAO recruitmentStudents under the banner of the Agriculture Degree Students’ Association have been staging protests across agricultural universities in the state. Dharwad/Shivamogga: With less than three weeks left for the Karnataka Examinations Authority’s (KEA) recruitment examination for Agriculture Officer (AO) and Assistant Agriculture Officer (AAO) posts, students of the University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad, have intensified their protest, demanding that the state government withdraw the recruitment notification and issue a fresh one. The government has notified recruitment for 945 Group-B AO and AAO posts in the Agriculture Department, with the examination scheduled for August 8 and 9. However, the inclusion of BE Biotechnology graduates and students from private agriculture colleges among the eligible candidates has sparked widespread opposition from agriculture students, who argue that the technical posts should be reserved exclusively for graduates with agriculture and allied agriculture degrees. Students under the banner of the Agriculture Degree Students’ Association have been staging protests across agricultural universities in the state.
